# Published aggregates from the crowdsourcing and language-learning study

Local version 1.0, reviewed 5 October 2026. Stage: `prepared_needs_deposit`. 166 selected published cells, not original questionnaire responses or a complete replication package.

Source: Çiler Hatipoğlu, Nihada Delibegović Džanić, Elżbieta Gajek and Lina Miloshevska (2022), Crowdsourcing and language learning habits and practices in Turkey, Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Republic of North Macedonia and Poland in the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods. DOI https://doi.org/10.4312/slo2.0.2022.2.132-183. UIST record: https://repository.uist.edu.mk/items/0de15561-ad68-4141-aa70-7268c6fcbe10. The source identifies Lina Miloshevska with UIST on PDF page 1. Its printed citation says pages 132–181; the DOI and downloaded PDF extend through 183. This discrepancy is retained, not silently resolved.

The CSV selects explicitly reported counts/percentages from Tables 1a/1b (PDF 12, printed 143), 2a (PDF 13, printed 144), 2b (PDF 14, printed 145) and 3 (PDF 17, printed 148). P1 is Spring 2020; P2 is Spring 2022. The source describes cross-cultural student questionnaires and descriptive quantitative/qualitative analysis. The source totals are 211 and 185 participants, but these totals must not be substituted for an unknown question-specific denominator.

Each selected cell was independently checked against rendered source tables. Table 1a prints RNM total 41 while adjacent prose says 42; table cells are retained without reconciliation. Its TUR female percentage has malformed typography 72.,1; the CSV normalizes it to 72.1 with an explicit note. Table 3 total 468 counts multiple-response resource mentions, not unique respondents. Categories are explicit; no missing categories/cells, respondent records, counts or denominators were inferred.

The source article specifies CC BY-SA 4.0 on PDF page 1. Proposed reuse retains that licence and share-alike condition, pending an item-specific rights decision. Source-study authors are attributed, with no endorsement implied. Accountable compiler/depositor is unassigned. The repository preparation agents transcribed cells and added documentation; they are not authorised source-study depositors.

The interrupted draft was preserved in local research history. Coordinator corrections added explicit gender response labels, corrected the source licence to CC BY-SA 4.0 and restored total-percentage precision (100.0). Source-value checks are in evidence/coordinator-validation.json. Researcher-supplied original data remain preferred.

No public dataset identifier, deposit date or actual depositor acceptance exists for this package. The responsible authorised depositor must confirm source authority, attribution, documentation, rights and access conditions and complete the normal DSpace deposit terms. No administrator review or sign-off is required. See release_checklist.md.
